comment: The pipeline's STAGES and which one may legally follow which. Data, not code, because
the Router composes a route out of it and a test has to be able to read the same thing.
This is NOT the ledger's legal-transition map. That map is about STATES, and it exists to
make one claim impossible to record — 'QA passed' from somewhere that is not a QA run.
This is about which WORK runs next, which is a routing question, and collapsing the two
would put a guard on claims in the same file as a decision about throughput. They are
cross-checked instead: every stage's `state` here must be a real ledger state, and
tests/flow-graph.test.js walks each composable route through the state machine.
`always: true` marks a stage a route may not drop. The Router chooses how much
deliberation a ticket gets; it does not get to route around the gate or around intake.
`next` is FORWARD composition — what a route may put after this stage. `loops_to` is how a
failure comes back, which is not the same thing and must not be composable: review returns
to implement on a rejection, and a route reading `["qa", "implement"]` would otherwise
validate as if testing something before building it were a plan.

intake.why: trust, risk, dependencies and dedupe. Runs on every issue; nothing may skip it.

project.why: the once-per-repo architecture decision, before anything is split or planned. Always ends at a human, and that gate is not a config flag.

maintainer.why: splits an epic into issues, each of which gets its own route. Terminal for THIS issue.

plan.why: a feature is a design question. Emits the work order.

debug.why: a bug is a question about what a running system is doing, answered by reproducing it.

implement.why: applies a decided work order. Always followed by the gate.

gate.why: waits for whatever checks gate this PR. A route may not skip verification.

review.why: reads the diff against the work order. Skippable on a trivial change.

qa.why: adversarial, live browser. The only stage that can run with no PR at all: routed alone it is an AUDIT, driven by issue number against what is already deployed.

root-cause.why: puts the previous diagnosis on trial after a QA failure or a repeated mechanical one.

on_complete.merge: the PR merges once every pre-merge claim re-establishes
on_complete.file-issue-only: no PR exists; every finding becomes its own issue
on_complete.comment-only: the artifact is posted for a person to read and the pipeline stops there
